title: 3-Read Friday #84: AI Formative Assessment, Teacher Training Pitfalls, and Fact Fluency
author: Craig Barton
summary: 3-Read Friday #84 leads with Becky Allen's experiment testing whether a free LLM can diagnose misconceptions from a photographed piece of student work, using a simple prompt she shares in the post. Jim Hewitt and Nidhi Sachdeva then take a deep dive into teacher CPD, offering five warning signs of a sales-pitch-style training session and concrete ways to push back. Dylan Kane closes with an AI-assisted worksheet series for building times-table fluency, using an approach Barton flags as squarely in his wheelhouse of AI-generated maths resources. Barton's own admission -- that he recognises himself falling for one of Hewitt and Sachdeva's five persuasion tactics -- gives the issue a candid throughline about staying critical of professional-development claims, including from AI.
points: Allen's experiment is the issue's most technically ambitious pick: testing whether a freely available LLM can analyse a photo of student work, identify misconceptions, and generate diagnostic follow-up questions.

Hewitt and Sachdeva's five sales-pitch tactics -- "research says," trust-the-expert, loaded language, the equity justification, and all-theory-no-evidence -- give teachers a checklist for pushing back on unsubstantiated CPD claims.

Barton's own confession -- admitting he has fallen for the first tactic on Hewitt and Sachdeva's list -- signals the issue's throughline of staying critically honest about persuasion, whether from a CPD facilitator or an AI tool.

Kane's fact-fluency worksheets close the loop on AI-in-practice, showing a teacher using AI not to replace pedagogical judgement but to generate the repetitive practice materials that judgement still has to design.
quotes: Becky describes a fascinating experience she had. She wrote a simple prompt (which she shares in the post) that enabled a freely available LLM to analyse a photo of students' work, identify possible misconceptions, and then write diagnostic questions to find more evidence for those misconceptions.
Jim and Nihdi take a deep dive into the world of teacher CPD, offering five warning signs to look out for, and actions you can take as recipients of that CPD.
I'll admit to falling foul of the first one on their list myself.
Regular readers know I love a bit of AI Maths resource creation. So, I loved Dylan’s post about a series of worksheets he has created using AI to help students develop fluency in their times tables.
